notes:
Account summary: Verdure builds real-time route optimization + customer-facing tracking. POC centered on reranking for ETA predictions + internal doc search for ops playbooks. Team is technically strong (platform + ML ops) but very cost sensitive — CFO wants tight unit economics before any commit.

Discovery highlights:
- 2025-10-08 initial intro (Liam): interested in replacing expensive in-house batching; asked for latency targets <120ms 95p for API calls.
- 2025-12-04 feasibility call w/ Priya: demo of dedicated instance demo; ops liked batching suggestions but flagged GPU costs and token billing.
- 2026-01-22 security sync: requested SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS integration details, audit log sample (ticket SEC-4472 opened).
- 2026-02-18 demo: ran contrived reranking POC (Fireflies ff_2026-02-18_verdure-demo-1). Early perf looked good, but finance pushed back on projected monthly spend at scale.
- 2026-03-01 procurement call: procurement said "we can't sign large annual commit without clearer unit-econ; smaller pilots preferred" (see ff_2026-03-01_security-call).

POC / Technical notes:
- POC workload: 100k monthly reranking calls, average 8-12 tokens per candidate, expected throughput spiky during morning batch windows.
- Latency requirement: 95th <120ms for single-turn reranking; some endpoints can tolerate 200–300ms.
- Preferred models: efficient quantized Llama variants or Redwood-curated 7B/13B; team open to further quantization but worried about quality regressions.
- Routing needs: fallbacks to cheaper 4-bit models during cost spikes; prefer policy-based routing and prefix caching.

Commercial / Econ feedback:
- Procurement: wants smaller commit (~$20k/mo) with automatic step-ups; current Redwood reserved min commit modeled at $60k/mo for required throughput.
- Finance requested per-1000-call unit price and GPU-hour breakdown; asked for recalculation with batching gains assumed (we provided an initial model but they wanted more conservative numbers).
- Key quote from CFO: "If we can't bring marginal cost per customer session below $0.05 we don't have a path."

Why stalled / risks:
- Unit economics gap: our projected per-call cost (with conservative batching) still ~25–40% above their target at anticipated scale.
- No clear internal champion: Head of ML (evangelist) has limited procurement influence; procurement owns spend decisions and is risk-averse.
- Competitor pressure: competitor offered 6-month pilot with aggressive promotional pricing; Verdure is leaning toward short-term cost savings.

Suggested next moves (sales playbook):
- Rebuild econ model with three scenarios: conservative, expected, aggressive; show sensitivity to batching and caching; include a capped pilot option with strict usage limits.
- Propose a 3-month pilot for one region with $20k cap and defined SLOs; Redwood to commit to rollback plan + model-quality guardrails.
- Engage finance with an explicit GPU-hour / token breakdown and a side-by-side with competitor offer (ask them to share the competitor T&Cs).
- Internal: assign a Champion Enablement call for Head of ML to arm them for procurement discussions.

Open questions from account:
- Will Redwood accept smaller, capped pilots without annual commit? (Procurement)
- Can we provide a guaranteed max per-call cost if batching patterns are achieved? (Finance)
- Is custom quantization + fine-tuning on-prem an option to reduce token costs? (Head of ML)

Short-term status: Stalled in procurement review — account responsive to technical follow-ups but procurement silent on pricing concessions. Recommended: pause aggressive resource allocation until pilot parameters are negotiated.

Stated next-step owner: Liam to re-run econ model + send pilot term sheet by 2026-03-12.

Internal notes (AE tips):
- Be explicit about what we can and cannot change on pricing; procurement hates surprises.
- Emphasize Optimize features (batching, prefix cache) with concrete numbers from their POC.
- Consider trialing dedicated reserved capacity for a single routing policy with a small commit to show tail latency vs cost tradeoffs.
